attributes.body_ja:
「上（うえ）は」はかなり古風（こふう）な表現（ひょうげん）で、(A) の結果（けっか）として何（なに）かが行（おこな）われることや考（かんが）えられることを表（あらわ）します。「(A) だから (B)」のような意味（いみ）で使（つか）われ、(B) には必（かなら）ず (A) の結果（けっか）として当（あ）たり前（まえ）、または必要（ひつよう）だとみなされる内容（ないよう）が入（はい）ります。

この「上（うえ）」は名詞（めいし）であり、副助詞（ふくじょし）の「は」と一緒（いっしょ）に使（つか）われます。この文型（ぶんけい）は (A) をすでに確定（かくてい）したものとして示（しめ）し、それを考慮（こうりょ）した後（あと）で (B) が成（な）り立（た）つことを示（しめ）します。

この表現（ひょうげん）は動詞（どうし）の普通形（ふつうけい）の後（あと）に置（お）かれます。

「上（うえ）は」はかなり古風（こふう）な表現（ひょうげん）なので、現代（げんだい）の日本語（にほんご）では「からには」や「以上（いじょう）は」などの類似（るいじ）表現（ひょうげん）が使（つか）われることが多（おお）いです。
attributes.body:
A fairly old-fashioned phrase, 上（うえ）は highlights that something is being done or considered as a result of (A). It may be interpreted as 'once (A), (B)', 'since (A), (B)', 'now that (A), (B)', or 'as long as (A), (B)'. In these meanings, (B) will always be something that is deemed as either obvious or necessary.

上（うえ） in this phrase is a noun, and will be attached to the adverbial particle は. This creates a literal meaning that is similar to 'over and above (A), (B)'. This 'over and above' has a similar nuance to 'with that said', or 'all things considered' in English, and just presents (A) as something that is finalized.

This structure follows verbs in the standard form.

Due to 上（うえ）は being quite old-fashioned, expressions like からには or 以上（いじょう）は will be heard more frequently in modern-day Japanese, and will carry a similar meaning.

attributes.description: What's the difference between からには, 以上, and 上は?

attributes.body: 上に and 上は share the same kanji but serve different grammatical roles. 上に expresses accumulation of traits or actions, as in 忙しい上に風邪もひいた (I’m busy, and on top of that I caught a cold). 上は introduces a conditional or resolved stance, as in 引き受けた上は最後までやる (Since I accepted it, I’ll see it through).

first_relatable.meaning: As well, Besides, In addition to

second_relatable.title: 上は

attributes.body: 以上② and 上は both express a conditional premise leading to a natural or expected outcome. Their meanings are very similar and often interchangeable, but 上は feels somewhat old-fashioned, while 以上② is more common in modern usage. Both are relatively formal and typical of written language or structured speech.

first_relatable.title: 以上 ②
first_relatable.meaning: Since, Now that, As long as, If

second_relatable.title: 上は
second_relatable.meaning: Once, Since, Now that, As long as

attributes.body: 上は and からには both present a situation or condition, then express something deemed necessary or natural based on that situation. For example: 日本に来たからには、たくさんの日本人と話したい (Since I came to Japan, I want to speak to many Japanese people). The primary difference is formality: 上は is used almost exclusively in formal writing, while からには is common in both writing and everyday conversation.

first_relatable.title: 上は
first_relatable.meaning: Once, Since, Now that, As long as

attributes.body: 以来 and 上は can both be translated as since, but their usage is quite different. 以来 means since in the sense of time, as in 日本に来て以来、毎日日本語を使っている (Since coming to Japan, I use Japanese every day). 上は means since as in because of the given situation, as in 日本に来た上は、たくさんの日本人と話したい (Since I came to Japan, I want to speak to many Japanese people).
